lessons.title: Although + subject + verb
lessons.content: 'Although' is used to show contrast between two clauses. It is followed by a subject and verb. 'Although' can come at the beginning or middle of a sentence.

details.explanation: 'Although' at the start of a sentence connects two contrasting ideas.
details.example: Although she ran very fast, she lost the race.

details.explanation: 'Although' connects contrasting clauses even when both are complete sentences.
details.example: Although it rained all day, we enjoyed the party very much.

details.explanation: 'Although' can also appear at the end of a sentence.
details.example: They are generous although they are poor.
details.burmese: သူတို့ ဆင်းရဲပေမယ့် ပေးကမ်းစွန့်ကြဲတတ်ကြတယ်။

lessons.title: In spite of + noun / Ving
lessons.content: 'In spite of' is used to show contrast and is followed by a noun or a gerund (Ving). It has the same meaning as 'although' but requires a different structure.

details.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase to show contrast.
details.example: In spite of their quarrel, they remain the best of friends.
details.burmese: ရန်ဖြစ်ထားပေမယ့်ပဲ အကောင်းဆုံး သငယ်ချင်းဖြစ်နေကြတန်ပါ။

details.explanation: 'In spite of' can show contrast with a simple noun.
details.example: We went out in spite of the rain.
details.burmese: မိုးရွာပေမယ့်ပဲ ငါတို့ အပြင်ထွက်ခဲ့တယ်။

details.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a gerund (-ing form) when the contrast involves an action.
details.example: In spite of completing his master's degree, he could not find a quality job.
details.burmese: မောစတာဘွဲ့ရပေမယ့်ပဲ သူ အလုပ်ကောင်းကောင်း မရခဲ့ဘူး။
